title: Product of Array Except Self
prompt: Return products of every number except the current one, without division.
idea: Multiply what is on the left, then what is on the right. Zero values need no special case.
steps: For [1,2,3,4], left products are [1,1,2,6].
Walk backward with right products 1,4,12,24.
Multiply at each position to obtain [24,12,8,6].
complexity: O(n) time · O(1) extra space excluding output
solution:
def solve(nums):
    result = [1] * len(nums)
    product = 1
    for i, value in enumerate(nums):
        result[i] = product
        product *= value
    product = 1
    for i in range(len(nums)-1, -1, -1):
        result[i] *= product
        product *= nums[i]
    return result

title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
prompt: Return the minimum in a nonempty rotated ascending array of distinct values.
idea: Compare the middle with the right edge to identify which half contains the rotation.
steps: [4,5,6,7,0,1,2]: middle 7 exceeds right 2.
The minimum must be to the right of 7.
Narrow until the two search boundaries meet at 0.
complexity: O(log n) time · O(1) space
solution:
def solve(nums):
    l, r = 0, len(nums)-1
    while l < r:
        m = (l+r)//2
        if nums[m] > nums[r]: l = m+1
        else: r = m
    return nums[l]

prompt: Return target index or -1 in a rotated sorted array of distinct integers.
idea: One half is always sorted; use its boundary values to decide whether to search it.
steps: For [4,5,6,7,0,1,2], middle 7 has a sorted left half.
Target 0 is outside [4,7], so search right.
Repeat the same decision until target is found.

title: 3Sum
prompt: Return unique triplets summing to zero, sorted internally and in lexicographic order.
idea: Sorting lets two pointers move predictably while duplicate skipping avoids repeated answers.
steps: Fix -1 and move left/right pointers to find [-1,-1,2] and [-1,0,1].
Skip repeated fixed and pointer values.
complexity: O(n²) time · O(n) sorting space plus output
solution:
def solve(nums):
    nums = sorted(nums)
    result = []
    for i in range(len(nums)-2):
        if i and nums[i] == nums[i-1]: continue
        l, r = i+1, len(nums)-1
        while l < r:
            total = nums[i]+nums[l]+nums[r]
            if total < 0: l += 1
            elif total > 0: r -= 1
            else:
                result.append([nums[i],nums[l],nums[r]])
                l += 1; r -= 1
                while l < r and nums[l] == nums[l-1]: l += 1
    return result

title: Container With Most Water
prompt: Return the maximum water area between two vertical lines. Heights are nonnegative.
idea: The shorter wall limits the water; moving the taller wall cannot improve it.
steps: Start at both ends of [1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7].
Move the shorter left wall to 8; width 7 × height 7 = 49.
Continue inward, recording the best area.
complexity: O(n) time · O(1) space
solution:
def solve(height):
    l, r, best = 0, len(height)-1, 0
    while l < r:
        best = max(best, (r-l)*min(height[l],height[r]))
        if height[l] < height[r]: l += 1
        else: r -= 1
    return best

    for i,n in enumerate(nums): result ^= i ^ n

title: Decode Ways
prompt: Count decodings of a digit string using 1→A through 26→Z. Zero cannot stand alone; empty input returns 0.

6, or 2
A single 0 adds no paths.

def solve(s):

    a,b = 1,int(s[0] != '0')
    for i in range(1,len(s)):
        current = b if s[i] != '0' else 0
        if 10 <= int(s[i-1:i+1]) <= 26: current += a
        a,b = b,current
    return b

title: Linked List Cycle
prompt: Build a list from values; tail points to index pos, or null for -1. Return whether there is a cycle.
idea: A fast pointer eventually catches a slow pointer inside a cycle.
steps: Connect the tail to pos if pos is nonnegative.
Move slow once and fast twice.
Meeting proves a cycle; reaching null proves none.
complexity: O(n) time · O(n) adapter space; O(1) detection space
solution:
def solve(values, pos):
    class Node:
        def __init__(self,v): self.v=v; self.next=None
    nodes=[Node(v) for v in values]
    for a,b in zip(nodes,nodes[1:]): a.next=b
    if nodes and pos>=0: nodes[-1].next=nodes[pos]
    slow=fast=nodes[0] if nodes else None
    while fast and fast.next:
        slow=slow.next; fast=fast.next.next
        if slow is fast: return True
    return False

title: Remove Nth Node From End
prompt: Remove the nth node from the end of a linked-list traversal, returned as an array. 1 <= n <= length.
idea: Two pointers separated by n positions identify the predecessor of the node to delete.
steps: Build a dummy head before the list.
Move fast n steps, then advance slow and fast until fast reaches the tail.
Bypass slow.next and read the resulting traversal.
complexity: O(n) time · O(n) adapter space; O(1) deletion space
solution:
def solve(values, n):
    class Node:
        def __init__(self,v=0,nxt=None): self.v,self.next=v,nxt
    dummy=Node(); tail=dummy
    for v in values: tail.next=Node(v); tail=tail.next
    fast=slow=dummy
    for _ in range(n): fast=fast.next
    while fast.next: slow=slow.next; fast=fast.next
    slow.next=slow.next.next
    result=[]; node=dummy.next
    while node: result.append(node.v); node=node.next
    return result

title: Reorder List
prompt: Return traversal in first,last,second,second-last order. Build a linked list and rearrange its nodes.
idea: Find the midpoint, reverse the second half, then weave the halves together.
steps: For 1→2→3→4→5, split after 3.
Reverse 4→5 to 5→4.
Alternate nodes to form 1→5→2→4→3.
complexity: O(n) time · O(n) adapter space; O(1) reordering space
solution:
def solve(values):
    class Node:
        def __init__(self,v): self.v=v; self.next=None
    nodes=[Node(v) for v in values]
    for a,b in zip(nodes,nodes[1:]): a.next=b
    if not nodes: return []
    head=slow=fast=nodes[0]
    while fast.next and fast.next.next: slow=slow.next; fast=fast.next.next
    second=slow.next; slow.next=None; prev=None
    while second:
        nxt=second.next; second.next=prev; prev=second; second=nxt
    first=head; second=prev
    while second:
        a,b=first.next,second.next
        first.next=second; second.next=a; first=a; second=b
    result=[]
    while head: result.append(head.v); head=head.next
    return result

title: Word Search
prompt: Return whether word can be traced through orthogonally adjacent cells, using each cell at most once per path. Empty word returns true.
idea: Explore one matching character at a time and undo visited marks when returning.
steps: Match the first character at each possible starting cell.
Mark that cell and search neighbors for the next character.
Backtrack by removing the mark so a different path can reuse the cell.
complexity: O(rows × cols × 4^L) time · O(L) search space
solution:
def solve(board, word):
    if not word: return True
    if not board or not board[0]: return False
    m,n=len(board),len(board[0]); seen=set()
    def dfs(r,c,i):
        if i==len(word): return True
        if not (0<=r<m and 0<=c<n) or (r,c) in seen or board[r][c]!=word[i]: return False
        seen.add((r,c))
        found=any(dfs(x,y,i+1) for x,y in ((r+1,c),(r-1,c),(r,c+1),(r,c-1)))
        seen.remove((r,c)); return found
    return any(dfs(r,c,0) for r in range(m) for c in range(n))

Read digits up to # to get the next length.
Consume exactly that many characters and repeat.
complexity: O(total characters) time · O(total characters) space
solution:
def solve(words):
    encoded=''.join(str(len(w))+'#'+w for w in words)
    result=[]; i=0
    while i<len(encoded):
        j=encoded.index('#',i); size=int(encoded[i:j]); i=j+1
        result.append(encoded[i:i+size]); i+=size
    return result
